hook.text: HIV hides inside your DNA. Drugs suppress it but can't remove it. CRISPR might cut the virus out of the genome.

buildup.text: Some people are naturally HIV-resistant due to a mutation in CCR5—the receptor HIV uses to enter cells.

discovery.text: Scientists used CRISPR to disable CCR5 in patient cells, mimicking the natural resistance. Early trials showed promise.

twist.text: Excision BioTherapeutics tested cutting HIV DNA directly from infected cells in primates.

climax.text: A cure for HIV—not just management—may be possible. CRISPR attacks the virus where drugs can't reach: inside your DNA.

punchline.text: HIV hides in your genome. CRISPR can find it there.

quiz.question: Why is CCR5 important in HIV resistance?
options: It's the receptor HIV uses to enter cells
